correctness.rationale: The dissipativity identity forces every peripheral eigenoperator into the rank-one projector commutant, whose even block is diagonal. Because the hypercube parity incidence Gram matrix connects all even vertices through Hamming-distance-two links, this even diagonal is scalar; the remaining odd block is arbitrary only on ker T. Walsh-character eigenvalues and parity pairing prove dim ker T=binom(d,d/2)/2 for even d, zero for odd d. Hilbert–Schmidt contraction excludes defective zero eigenvalues and the parity block identity excludes nonzero imaginary frequencies, establishing convergence to the explicitly computed orthogonal conditional expectation. The localized return and 2/(pi d) constant follow from even-translation transitivity and Stirling. The standalone program independently constructs generators and checks ranks, limits, and finite-time evolution for d=1,...,6.

value.rationale: The natural partial-monitoring question has an exact dimension-parity transition on a canonical highly connected network: monitoring half the vertices destroys all preparation memory in odd dimensions yet leaves an exponentially large coherent protected matrix block in even dimensions. A localized unmonitored state then has a sharp polynomial 2/(pi d) return instead of the exponential 2^(-d) return in odd dimension or full-site dephasing. The all-state operator-limit theorem resolves preserved coherences, not merely the existence of dark eigenvectors; the exact physical invariant is a motivating, reusable benchmark for selective decoherence.
